item.text: I’ve got enough direct material. I’m stopping the search now and synthesizing the strongest claim-level evidence, with the main gap being that there’s little direct proof on day-to-day health/education/social-service administration beyond cabinet picks and welfare delivery channels.

**6B.4 research note for Srettha Thavisin, 2024**

Verdict: **mixed, leaning negative**. I found some real technocratic and rules-based delivery, but the strongest cabinet and program-design evidence still points to political-network staffing and broad, politically salient cash transfers rather than a consistently professional social-services model.

- [Thailand's Cabinet Reshuffle Welcomes Six New Ministers](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/52/iid/283531) | Public Relations Department | 29 Apr 2024 | Srettha moved [Pichai Chunhavajira](/) into Finance and Deputy PM; Pichai is described as former chair of the Stock Exchange of Thailand board. This is the clearest technocratic staffing signal in the 2024 fiscal apparatus and supports professional management at the funding end of social policy. IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`.

- [Special Envoy of ASEAN Chair on Myanmar welcomes successful pilot project of humanitarian initiative between Thailand and Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 26 Mar 2024 | Thailand’s border relief was run through the Thai Red Cross, Myanmar Red Cross, local communities, and the AHA Centre, with an explicit goal of transparent and effective delivery. This is strong evidence for competent, rules-based humanitarian administration rather than patronage. IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`.

- [Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs and IO representatives discuss Thailand and Myanmar border situation and explore further possible humanitarian cooperation](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm-chairs-hm-asst-mtg-260424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 26 Apr 2024 | Thailand coordinated with UNHCR, UNOCHA, IOM, UNICEF, WFP, UNDP, and ICRC to upscale assistance for people in need along the border. This is direct evidence that vulnerable populations were being served through professional humanitarian institutions. IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`.

- [Forty Thai senators seek PM's dismissal over cabinet appointment](https://theprint.in/world/forty-thai-senators-seek-pms-dismissal-over-cabinet-appointment/2089532/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 17 May 2024 | Senators challenged Srettha over the appointment of Pichit Chuenban, a lawyer with a bribery-related contempt history. That is the clearest patronage-network signal in the 2024 cabinet story and cuts against a clean technocratic reading. IDs: `6B.4`.

- [Thailand's Cabinet Reshuffle Welcomes Six New Ministers](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/52/iid/283531) | Public Relations Department, Kingdom of Thailand | 29 Apr 2024 | Dr Cholnan Srikaew was replaced as Public Health Minister by Somsak Thepsutin. That looks more like coalition/political staffing than a technocratic upgrade in a major social-service portfolio. IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`.

- [Thailand approves 135 billion baht digital wallet handout](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) | Reuters via Investing.com | 23 Apr 2024 | The 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million people was broad and politically salient, but Reuters said it drew immediate debt and fiscal-risk criticism. That is social-protection evidence, but it weakens the case for disciplined, professionally managed social spending. IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`.

Search gap: I did **not** find direct evidence on professional staffing or patronage in the day-to-day management of education, water/sanitation, housing, or child/elderly service agencies under Srettha. The record is mostly indirect: cabinet choices, fiscal-management choices, and humanitarian delivery channels.
